findings.title: Error IDs are paired with nodestore data by dict ordering
findings.body: `fetch_error_details` builds `node_ids` from `error_ids`, calls `nodestore.backend.get_multi(node_ids)` and then does `zip(error_ids, events.values())`. `get_multi` returns a mapping keyed by node id; its iteration order is not guaranteed to match the order of the input list (and backends may omit/reorder keys, e.g. when some come from cache). As a result an `ErrorEvent` can be built with the id of one error and the title/message/timestamp of a different one, and if any node is missing the remaining pairings shift by one. The ids/messages that end up in the Seer prompt and in the summary can therefore be wrong. Iterate over `node_ids` and look up `events[node_id]` instead of relying on dict order.

findings.title: Error/replay timestamps compared in different units, so errors are never interleaved
findings.body: `gen_request_data` compares `error_events[error_idx]["timestamp"]` with `event.get("timestamp", 0)`. Error timestamps come from nodestore event data, which is Unix time in **seconds**, while rrweb replay event timestamps are Unix time in **milliseconds**. Every error timestamp is therefore smaller than every replay event timestamp, so all error log lines are flushed before the first breadcrumb instead of being interleaved chronologically — defeating the purpose of this change. The unit tests hide this because the fixture segment uses second-scale timestamps (1.5, 2.0). Normalize both to the same unit (e.g. multiply error timestamps by 1000) before comparing.

findings.title: error_ids silently dropped when caller passes `field` query params
findings.body: `process_raw_response(snuba_response, fields=request.query_params.getlist("field"))` filters the replay payload down to the requested fields, and then `error_ids` is read from the filtered response. Any caller that supplies `?field=...` without `error_ids` (a legal request for this endpoint signature) will get `error_ids = []` and lose all error context with no indication why. Read `error_ids` from the unfiltered snuba response, or hardcode the field list used for this internal lookup.

findings.title: Feature-flagged table path renders an empty table, discarding widget data
findings.body: When `organization.features.includes('use-table-widget-visualization')` is true, the widget renders `<TableWidgetVisualization columns={[]} tableData={{data: [], meta: {fields: {}, units: {}}}} />` — the actual `result`/`fields`/`meta` for the widget are ignored. Any organization with the flag enabled will see every dashboard table widget render with no headers and no rows. Either pass the real `result` data/columns or don't wire the flag up until the mapping exists.

findings.title: Inconsistent optional chaining will throw when meta is absent
findings.body: `Object.keys(tableData?.meta.fields)` guards `tableData` but not `meta`, so if `tableData` is supplied without `meta` (the type requires it, but callers pass loosely-typed API data) this throws `Cannot read properties of undefined`. Elsewhere in the same component `tableData?.data ?? []` is defensive, so the intent was clearly to tolerate missing data. Use `tableData?.meta?.fields ?? {}`.

findings.title: Header alignment computed from display name instead of column key
findings.body: `fieldAlignment(column.name, column.type)` uses the human-readable column name. When callers override `name` (the documented use case, e.g. `name: 'Count of Span Duration'` for key `count(span.duration)`), `fieldAlignment` can no longer recognize the aggregate/field and will align numeric columns as if they were strings. Pass `column.key` to `fieldAlignment` and keep `column.name` only for the rendered label.

findings.title: age/timestamp mutual-exclusion checks use truthiness, so 0 values bypass validation
findings.body: `validate_timestamp` rejects a report when `self.initial_data.get("age")` is truthy and `validate_age` when `timestamp` is truthy. `age: 0` (a report generated just now, which is the common case for freshly queued reports) and `timestamp: 0` are falsy, so a report containing both fields is accepted when one of them is 0, and conversely the validation message is never triggered for the most frequent values. Compare against `None` (`is not None`) instead of truthiness.

findings.title: One invalid report in a batch discards the entire batch
findings.body: The loop returns HTTP 422 as soon as any single report in the posted array fails validation, so none of the valid reports in that batch are counted by the `browser_reporting.raw_report_received` metric. Browsers batch multiple reports per request and will keep re-sending the same batch, so a single malformed/unsupported report (e.g. a non-RFC URL, or a type outside `BROWSER_REPORT_TYPES`) permanently blinds the collector for that client. Prefer skipping+logging invalid entries and still processing the valid ones.

findings.title: get_environment_info issues a Snuba/nodestore fetch per issue in PR comments
findings.body: `get_environment_info` calls `issue.get_recommended_event()` for every issue included in a merged-PR comment (up to 5 per comment, for both GitHub and GitLab workflows). `get_recommended_event` runs a Snuba query plus a nodestore fetch, so each PR comment now performs several extra round trips in the comment task that previously only used the already-loaded `Group` rows. Consider fetching the latest/recommended events in bulk, or deriving the environment from data already available on the group.

findings.title: Issue template embeds a trailing newline while callers also join with newlines
findings.body: `MERGED_PR_SINGLE_ISSUE_TEMPLATE` ends with `\n`, but both `GitHubPRCommentWorkflow.get_comment_body` and `GitlabPRCommentWorkflow.get_comment_body` join the rendered lines with `"\n"`. The posted comment therefore contains a blank line between every issue and an extra blank line before the footer (visible in the updated test expectations). If the double spacing is not intended, drop the trailing newline from the template.

findings.title: Analytics event recorded before the feature flag / validation checks
findings.body: `analytics.record("preprod_artifact.api.assemble", ...)` runs before the `organizations:preprod-artifact-assemble` feature check and before any schema validation, so every request from orgs without the feature (and every malformed request) is counted as an assemble call. This inflates the metric and makes it useless for measuring real usage; move the record after the feature gate, or add a flag/result attribute.

findings.title: 60s processing deadline may be too short for a 100-identity auth refresh chunk
findings.body: `check_auth_identities` iterates over up to `chunk_size=100` identities, each performing a network `provider.refresh_identity(...)`, and then re-schedules `check_auth` to continue the chain. With a 60s processing deadline the task can be killed mid-batch; because `check_auth` already bumped `last_synced` for the whole chunk before enqueuing, those identities are skipped for ~a day and, more importantly, the follow-up `check_auth.apply_async` at the end of the function never runs, so the batching chain stops. Size the deadline to the worst case (chunk_size × per-identity refresh latency) or make the reschedule happen before the refresh loop.

findings.title: attributes can now be undefined and query defaults changed
findings.body: The rewritten hook returns `attributes: isFetching ? previous : data`, where `data` is `TagCollection | undefined`; previously the hook always returned an object (`{}` at minimum), so consumers that spread/iterate the result (e.g. building filter key sections) can now receive `undefined` on error or before the first fetch. Additionally, the move from `useApiQuery` (which set `retry: false`, `refetchOnWindowFocus: false`) to a bare `useQuery` reinstates the default retry/refetch-on-focus behaviour, and the `environment` parameter that was previously sent is now dropped. Default `data` to `{}` and re-apply the query options if the previous behaviour was intended.

findings.title: No-op migrations point at a replacement migration that is not in this change
findings.body: Both 0917 and 0920 are gutted with the comment "See 0921_convert_org_saved_searches_to_views_rerevised.py for the correct migration", but no such file is added in this PR. If 0921 does not exist, the org saved-search → view backfill is now silently never performed and the comment misleads the next reader. Add the replacement migration (or fix the reference).
